title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: US stock futures tumbled overnight as early returns pointed to a Democratic sweep of the House and Senate — Nasdaq 100 futures fell ~2%, S&P 500 futures ~1%, Dow futures ~400+ points — extending Tuesday's AI-driven selloff.

Markets: Tuesday's cash close was mixed ahead of the vote (Dow -0.4%, Nasdaq +0.8%, S&P 500 +0.4%), while Brent crude slid toward $104 after Trump said the US will cut off military aid to Israel by year-end.
Companies: Apple fell 2% on weak margin guidance from high memory costs, letting Nvidia reclaim the title of world's most valuable company.
Companies: Apollo Global Management swung to a $1B+ Q3 net loss (shares -5%); Meta is paying a steep ~1.6-point yield premium on a new $4B bond sale to fund its AI buildout.
Companies: Anthropic's IPO prep looks strong even as AI-linked stocks get hammered (CoreWeave down >40% in a month); OpenAI's latest funding round valued it at $1.25T, short of its $1.4T target.
Macro/Policy: JPMorgan estimates a Democratic 'blue wave' could knock ~0.5% off the S&P 500 as investors brace for policy uncertainty while full midterm results land.
Macro/Policy: Wednesday's calendar: ADP jobs report, trade balance and PMI data, plus earnings from AMD, Qualcomm, Uber, Pfizer, CVS Health and McDonald's.
